subject: Data residency & private-link operational map — confirmation and runbook items
messages:
From: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@medicore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify EU-only hosting + private-link controls (ops details requested)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the SOC 2 packet — helpful. Our legal and infra teams dug into the hosting notes and want a short operational mapping showing exactly where data paths may touch non-EU endpoints for the Private deployment option. Specifically we need:

- A diagram or table that shows the control plane vs data plane locations and any supporting services that may be in US zones (monitoring, billing, telemetry).
- Confirmation that customer data, model weights, and KV caches for our tenant will persist only in EU-hosted instances and storage.
- Details on the private link (Privatelink/privatelink-like) design: peerings, NAT/egress behaviors, and whether any fallbacks to hosted (shared) tiers could route traffic outside EU if capacity is constrained.

Can you also attach any short ops runbook or matrix that the on-call team would follow to validate geo-boundary during incident response? We don’t need full manuals — just the checklist and the locations for keys/keystore rotation.

Goal is to close our geography design review this week. Appreciate a concise confirmation and any supporting files we can include in the audit packet.

Thanks —
Alice
Alice Yuan
Head of Security, MediCore Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@medicore.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify EU-only hosting + private-link controls (ops details requested)

Hi Alice —

Thanks — and great questions. Short version up front: for Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC + private link peering) we operate a split control/data plane where the customer data plane (model serving, storage, KV cache) is pinned to the customer-chosen EU region and does not egress to US/other regions under normal operation. The control plane (service orchestration, billing records) runs in a separate control cluster which may be hosted in a different region for redundancy but we can provide a EU-only control plane option as part of the Private deployment contract.

What I attached: a one-page "private_link_matrix" (XLSX) that maps peering endpoints, expected IP ranges, and services that terminate in the EU data plane vs services that are control-plane-only. I also attached an abbreviated ops runbook PDF (ops-runbook-dataplane-v1.3.pdf) that contains the incident checklist you requested. Highlights below: 

- Data plane: models, logs marked as customer-data, KV caches, and object storage are instantiated in the EU tenant cluster. Persistent storage volumes are backed by EU-region block/object stores.
- Cryptographic keys: Customer keystores (HSM/KMS) can be customer-managed in their EU project or we can integrate with the customer's KMS—either way keys used for data-plane encryption do not leave EU storage boundaries.
- Private link: peering is established via a single-mapped private endpoint per tenant. There is no default internet egress from the peered subnet; NAT/egress is controlled by the tenant route table.
- Fallbacks: The serving runtime has a validated fallback policy that only uses alternative model variants in the same region. Cross-region fallback to hosted shared pools is only enabled if explicitly allowed in your config; by default we disable cross-region fallbacks for customers that require strict residency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jonas — please review the two attachments for any operational gaps (routing, peering CIDR, monitoring hooks) and confirm the checklist items.
2) Marissa — I’ll need a short contract addendum text confirming EU-only control plane option and a contact at procurement to sign.
3) Alice — if this looks good I can produce a formal EU residency letter we can countersign.

I included the attachments and a Drive link with the full runbook. If you want a diagram exported as a PNG for your audit packet I can add that as well.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 12:35:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify EU-only hosting + private-link controls (ops details requested)

Looping in a couple of quick confirmations after I reviewed the attachments: 

- Private_link_matrix.xlsx: IP ranges and service endpoints verified for EU node pools. I added a short column ("monitoring-host-region") indicating where metrics aggregation occurs — by default metrics from EU data plane are ingested into a regional metrics cluster in EU. Aggregated digests we ship to control-plane analytics are pseudonymized and contain no raw customer inputs.
- ops-runbook-dataplane-v1.3.pdf: Updated step 4.2 to note the exact CLI command to validate peering state and the path to the keystore inventory. I also added a short troubleshooting step for stuck KV cache shards during tenant restart.

One operational caveat worth surfacing to customers: if they request cross-region disaster recovery replication (active-standby in another region) that requires explicit agreement and is treated as a separate offering — replication traffic will be documented and encrypted, but it is cross-region by definition.

Irene, Marissa — I flagged two minor redline suggestions in the XLSX comments (peering TTL and monitoring retention). If approved I can prepare a tight paragraph for the residency letter that covers the fallback and replication caveats.

-Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@medicore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify EU-only hosting + private-link controls (ops details requested)

Thanks, Irene / Jonas — this is exactly what we needed. The matrix and runbook are clear; we’ll include the XLSX and ops runbook in our internal audit packet. Two follow-ups before we close: 

1) Can you produce a one-paragraph residency letter we can store with contracts that explicitly states "control plane" vs "data plane" locations and affirms that, without an explicit DR replication request, no customer data leaves the EU data plane?
2) Procurement will ask for the EU-only control plane option as a checkbox in the SOW. Marissa — our procurement lead will reach out to you for the specific SOW clause and pricing delta.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can send the residency paragraph and the PNG diagram today we’ll get this across the finish line.

Best,
Alice
